killedBy: classifyPad: how a pad is matched lets the browser's own 'standard' win over a catalogue entry that would also match
classifyPad: the four verdicts reads a browser-remapped pad as standard, and hands back the standard profile
why: Breaks the order contract by making the standard-mapping branch unreachable, so every pad -- including one the browser has already remapped -- falls through to the catalogue search. That is how issue #596's 'standard-mapped controllers retain current behavior' criterion dies quietly later: the shipped catalogue is empty today so the damage is total and obvious, but once issue #606 adds an entry, a loose matcher would capture working Xbox and PlayStation pads and re-lay them out. The order is what makes a catalogue entry unable to do that, at any looseness.
